reviews.text: Sweet little stopover on the way to Zhangjiajie. We were lucky to go on off-peak season, so we didn't have to queue for the shuttle bus up to the lake. The boat trip lasts around half an hour and you drift by beautiful mountain scenes and they have a couple of indigenous boats that have singers serenade you with local songs as you float by. There are also some resident comorants perched up with a fisherman. There is lovely waterfall down the bottom and a pond with salamanders (admittedly it would be nicer to see them in a more suitable enclosure, as they are a lot larger than I imagined!!) It would have been nice to spend more time in the area to appreciate any hikes.

I got the coach here as part of my group tour. We went on the boat on the lake which was amazing. The views were breathtaking as it is surrounded by mountains. There were people on the lake who would sing or interact with this which made the experience more interactive. If you're visiting Zhangjiajie, I highly recommend coming to the lake. If you go in the morning there will be less queues for the boats. It is also worth walking around the entrance that leads up to the lake. There you will find a small performance, Monkey King statue, people dresses in traditional Xi'an clothing and a giant salamander enclosure.

Scenery is good, for 20 minutes boat ride. We don’t need to queue. There are locals sings while you passed the area. Lake is very clean, deep turquoise color like glass. There is Sun Wu Kong statue near the waterfall and salamander park. It’s cool but I think Tianmen Mountain is more worthy to visit 😉

If it's compared to the great Tianmen and Tianzi Mountain, Baofeng lake is just ok. The trip was short and there's waterfall nearby, the shooting location from Journey to the West film. If you have tight schedule, you can skip it

Do something else. The waterfall, the lake, the everything is made up. The boat ride is 20 mins with 30 seconds of someone singing -which you can barely hear. The staff is nice, but they can only do so much on a lake from a dam. Save your money, just go back to Zangjiajia or Tianmen. Literally anything else in the area is a good us eof your long trip to get here.

Really, skip this if you must. Not worth the entrance fee. They do not offer concessional tkts to foreign seniors - a real scam as in general Chinese attractions do not discriminate as such. Even the signboards do not state as such. Short cruise, long queues, smallish lake, sceneries not particularly impressive.

Honestly, quite disappointing. The whole thing felt really fake - the actual lake is artificial so it just looks like an unatural flooded valley - becasue it is (and probably caused a ton of environmental damage). And then you go round on the boat past some people in costumes singing, which I know is symbolic and traditional but the way you just go past looking at them feels really inauthentic, like you're on a theme park ride. It was pretty I guess. I went in mid March and all the walking paths were closed, so literally the only thing you can do is go on a 5 minute bus, 20 minute boat and then bus back. There's a waterfall section with museum too but that's so small it can be seen in way less than 30 mins. So for ¥95 (for entry plus boat) it was not good value, felt like an inauthentic theme park and just boring. Wish I'd gone back into Zhangjiajie National Park instead.
It is a high altitude lake. The water is very clear without pollution. Average depth is 72 m and the length is 2.5 km.

Shape imagination while enjoying the lake view along with different rocky mountains is the main adventure of the Chinese traditional boat journey through the lake. The lake has an average depth of 72 meter with an maximum depth of 169 meter approximately. Mountain love songs are one of sweetest parts to enjoy the boat journey, sung by male & female, individually, they wait in two separate cottages located at the feet of mountains & when any boat crosses their cottage they start to sing loud to cheer the tourists. It also includes a bus journey through the snaky mountain road. At the terminal point, there is also a natural flow of a large amount of water coming down to mountains feet. A small pond exists there, colorful fishes swim to get some adore from the cheerful tourists. A baby fish, age of almost 70, lives there in a pond, people gives him coins & notes to make fulfill the wishes they want. A baby fish lives nearly around 150 years of life span. It's about 4 feet in length & 12-15kg in weight. Moreover, you may have an amazing visit to Baofeng Lake for half a day if you plan to go there in near future.

Beautiful, scenic and picturesque lake in Wulingyuan, Zhangjiajie. If you go on a misty day, you can enjoy a Chinese landscape painting coming to life with the ethereal and mythical aura enclosing the locale. This is an artificial fresh-water reservoir created by blocking gorge and building dam in the 1970s

The key word here is if u don't have to queue....spent 30 mins queue to hop on a bus to enter. Quite disappointed as there were no translation available. Singing is there but the boat just passed by....salamander park is to see an endangered species held captive.

Came here as a top up to a tour package. Quite expensive and underwhelming for the price. I think it's a lake in a crater within the mountains, which is an experience in itself, but can skip as not worth the price.
Great experience and enjoyed the scenery and cultural aspect of the boat trip with 啊哥 and 啊妹 singing.

a tour in Baofeng Lake is a must. where you will enjoy the traditional boat ride at the heart of nature. This is Baofengs Lake, one of the most popular lakes close to Zhangjiajie Wulingyuan Park. During the ride, local singers will appear from some of the decks/balconies overlooking the lake and they will welcome you singing some traditional songs. The que was very long and we had to wait around 45 min to get in the ride.
it's quite small and not beautiful as I expexted, it does not worth the price too. You buy entrance ticket and shuttle bus ticket seperately, it's too expensive
Its a beautiful place to visit. Need English translation to understand the story that given by the local guide on board.Came in the afternoon to get a better view
Beautiful lake. A guide will be present during the boat ride, and she sang beautifully.

Nice boat ride around the lake whilst guide describes the scenery and gives you some insight into the local minority villagers customs. Takes about 30 minutes. You can walk up or take a bus. Enjoyable but not the most breath taking part of the area.

Avoid this place. Complete scam. We paid the “entrance fee” of 30 Yuan per person. They kept telling us to buy the ticket for the boat which we didn’t want to do. Except the boat and the bus ticket are together. Which is a ridiculous 110 Yuan per person. We entered and thought you can just walk to the lake, which you can’t because they blocked off the road and made it in accessible by foot. So we paid 60 Yuan for basically nothing. There was a little section of the lake that we did get to see and I would definitely not recommend spending the ridiculous price for the boat and bus ticket. Not worth the time and money at all. This place is the definition of complete scam.

Worthless, time stealing, there's much more beautiful around. Entrance fee almost 100RMB, all you do is jump on a bus, get in a boat, make a ridiculous 10min. circle and go back by bus. Additionally, there's some kitsch singing in traditional garment. Just stay away.

Baofeng Lake is 2 kilometers south of Suoxi Valley Nature Reserve. There is a deep and serene valley and the pellucid lake reflects a picture of verdant mountains. Here, the lake and the mountains serve as a foil to each other.Baefong Lake is a fresh water lake in the Wulingyuan Scenic Area near Zhangjiajie, Hunan Province, China. Its average depth is 72 metres (236 ft) and it is surrounded by forested stone peaks.

第七天 張家界 【寶峰湖遊船】-岳陽 【遠眺岳陽樓、洞庭湖、汴河街、巴陵廣場】-武漢 【寶峰湖遊船】主要景點由寶峰湖和鷹窩寨兩大塊組成。其中寶峰湖、奇峰飛瀑、鷹窩寨、一線天 被稱為武陵源「四絕」。是武陵源風景名勝中的精品景點,也是張家界核心景區惟一以水為主的旅遊景點。 【遠眺岳陽樓、洞庭湖】 岳陽樓位於湖南省岳陽市，緊靠洞庭湖畔，是江南三大名樓之一，因范仲 淹的《岳陽樓記》而聞名天下。登上岳陽樓，眼前便是煙波浩渺的八百里洞庭湖水，耳邊不由自主的迴盪起千古佳句“先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂”。除了登樓遙望思古，岳陽樓的建築構造也非常值得一看。全樓沒有用一根鐵釘和一道橫梁，樓頂形式十分獨特。 【汴河商業街】汴河街位於岳陽市岳陽樓區，靠近洞庭北路，是以岳陽樓文化、洞庭文化、巴陵文化為基礎打造的一條特色仿古商業街。這裡的建築設計古樸典雅，沿青石板路而行，兩側是客棧酒家茶社、戲台樓閣，皆為青瓦白牆。沿街還有許多美食小吃、工藝品小店，已成為岳陽的一條美食 街。 【巴陵廣場】 位於美麗的洞庭湖畔，附近就是岳陽美食街汴河街和岳陽樓公園，是岳陽最為熱鬧的 場所之一

장가계 관광의 서문을 열은 곳이었다 인공 호수이지만 참으로 아름다워 기억에 남아있다 길이가 대략 3km 수심 70여m의 작은 호수입니다 장사시 에서 장가계 쪽으로 4시간 여 버스로 갑니다 이른 아침 너무 아름다운 침봉 들을 만나며 안개 속을 달려 도착한 보봉 호수 입구에는 아릿다운 토가족 어린 아가시들이 정겹게 다가 옵니다 헉헉 대며 가파른 길을 따라 오른 댐의 정상엔 유람선이 가득합니다 엔진을 달지 않고 밧데리로 운행하는 작은 배들입니다 유람선을 타고 호수를 나가 모퉁이를 돌자 높고 청아한 토가족 아가시가 아주 작은 수변 정자에서 나와 알수 없는 노래를 부릅니다 가히 넋을 빼는 미모와 목소리입니다 ㅎㅎㅎㅎㅎ 호수 일주를 마치고 내려오는 길에는 토가족 여인 전통 복장을 한 아가시가 다가와 사진을 찍자 합니다 1000원이라 합니다 ㅎㅎㅎㅎㅎ
